name: Lexington Law
description_short: Lexington Law is a credit repair company that disputes errors and negative items on credit reports to help consumers improve their credit scores.
description_long:
Lexington Law operates as a credit repair firm focused on helping consumers identify and dispute inaccurate or negative items appearing on their credit reports. The company maintains a presence across most U.S. states and provides access to credit repair services through its website platform, with customer support available Monday through Friday during business hours (7am-4pm MST). Founded to address credit industry issues, the firm positions itself within the broader credit repair and consumer finance space.

The company's core service offering centers on credit dispute and repair. Lexington Law provides guidance on removing various negative items including late payments, charge-offs, repossessions, collections, judgments, foreclosures, medical bills, inquiries, and bankruptcies. They offer educational content on credit reports, credit scores, dispute letter processes, and debt collection laws. The company also provides a free credit assessment to evaluate clients' situations and offers multiple service tiers through their focus tracks model (specific details on pricing and track specifics were not accessible on their public website).

Lexington Law distinguishes itself through several operational features: they employ or work with lawyers (lawyer profiles are listed on their site), maintain corporate responsibility initiatives, and operate physical locations in multiple states. The company provides both chat-based agent support and formal client support channels. Their educational content library is extensive, covering not just dispute processes but also credit-building fundamentals, credit card and personal loan options for bad credit, and explanations of relevant credit laws.

A significant limitation is the lack of transparent pricing information on their public website—pricing pages return 404 errors, making it difficult for prospective clients to understand costs before engaging. The company's service hours are limited to weekday business hours, and they are not currently serving all U.S. states. While they position themselves as offering legal support, the actual scope of attorney involvement in individual cases is unclear from available public information.
pros: Offers free credit assessment to evaluate client situations before purchase
Employs or works with lawyers, providing potential legal backing for disputes
Extensive educational content covering dispute processes, credit laws, and credit-building strategies
Services available in most U.S. states with multiple physical locations
Multi-channel support including chat with agents and dedicated client support
Addresses specific negative item types (charge-offs, repossessions, foreclosures, medical bills, judgments, etc.)
Provides both dispute assistance and credit education resources on their blog
cons: Pricing information is not publicly available on website (pricing page returns 404 error)
Limited service hours (Monday-Friday, 7am-4pm MST only; closed weekends)
Not currently serving all U.S. states, limiting accessibility for some consumers
Focus tracks pricing structure and specific service tiers are not clearly detailed publicly
No transparent information about what attorney involvement clients receive in their service plans
best_for: Consumers with multiple negative items on credit reports seeking professional dispute assistance
Individuals who want legal backing for credit disputes and want to work with law firms
People needing guidance on specific negative items like collections, charge-offs, or judgments
diagnosis: Lexington Law is best for consumers seeking professional credit repair with legal support who have multiple negative items on their reports and can pay for the service. The main caveat is that transparent pricing is unavailable on their public website, requiring direct contact to understand costs, and their limited service hours and incomplete state coverage may not work for all consumers.
services: Removal of late payments from credit reports
